notes: T625 (stale pause kills a fresh dispatch) — test-first, red quoted against 2026-08-22 code, then green. THE DEFECT: D047, a `pause` issued 2026-08-20T12:55:28Z, carried its discharge condition ('T545 goes first') only in English prose inside --note; T545 closed done; nothing re-evaluated D047, so it kept killing fresh T544 dispatches (one mid-run poll kill at 741 s, one launch refusal) and every termination surfaced as verified=fail against deepseek-v4-pro and deepseek-v4-flash — two false model-failure rows. THREE MECHANISMS SHIPPED: (1) discharge-by-condition — `managent tell <t> pause --until-done <row>` writes the condition into the directive record (validated pause-only, T<id>, != target; ack preserves it); tools/directive_policy.py (new shared module, stdlib-only) evaluates it at every apply and bin/dispatch + tools/runner both use it, so the refusal and the enforcement agree; (2) staleness horizon — an unacked pause WITHOUT a condition older than WEIZIGO_DIRECTIVE_STALE_HOURS (default 24) is reported stale, not enforced; `kill` is never stale (an explicit halt must not expire); (3) self-identifying kills — tools/runner writes a run record with kill_class=directive at launch-time refusal (previously rc=124 + a log line, indistinguishable from a wall-kill), tools/dispatch_verify records verified=directive-kill reason=<id>/<type> (never verified=fail; model-profiles' close-event grading and orcha-acceptance AC6 both skip it), and bin/dispatch REFUSES to launch a row a pending directive would kill (nothing spawned — the D047 waste is gone). Heal policy: a pause-directive kill heals (reopens) with the directive id annotated; a KILL-directive death is NOT auto-healed — a stand-down must not be re-dispatched by the machinery (the D048 duplicate-dispatch risk). REGRESSION tools/regression-directive-kill.sh (wired into zig build test via build.zig): 12 arms — dispatch refusal (nothing spawned), empty-inbox null, until_done-done discharge, until_done-open enforcement, stale-not-enforced, launch-kill run record, verify classification (run-record + log fallback), wall-kill null, and three D021 arms using the REAL on-disk fixtures (t526/t615/t616 logs + run records — SKIP loudly on a fresh clone). COORDINATION with T544 (live on src/managent/main.zig for the attribution write-path fix): git log checked first — last main.zig commit ee28e62 (T522), worktree clean; my change is the directive region (Directive.until_done, tell/inbox/ack/display), T544's is claim/done attribution — no overlap. OUTCOME: T544 committed BOTH halves together in 8076156 ('T544: model-attribution write path + backfill'), message naming the T625 in-flight hunks (until_done/isTaskId/directive-discharge); D022 (recorded directive ID) asked whether to separate them — they are independent and both wanted, so no separation; the src/managent/main.zig deliverable is satisfied by that commit (worktree == HEAD, verified). D021 AMEND (recorded directive ID): T612's scope extension on the provider-refusal classifier — the grep-over-worker-output classifier missed 'hit your session limit' (5 Claude rows recorded fail) and matched quoted/prose content (T526 watchdog kill recorded unreached, T601 quota-prose). Fixed per D021: classification unit is now the run record first (a harness kill is not a refusal unless a refusal signature sits in the worker output's TAIL window — T616's session limit CAUSED its startup-timeout kill, T526's mid-log quote does not launder its watchdog kill); worker stdout treated as untrusted (refusal window = first/last 8 KiB of worker output, [runner] lines excluded); 'hit your session limit' added. CENSUS (docs/evidence/T625-directive-kill/census-2026-08-22.md, denominator 315 dispatch-verify rows): directive kills = 2 (both T544 2026-08-22; the 7 T544 rows dated 2026-08-20 are the documented host-memory-pressure cohort, not directive kills — the log accumulates); direction B (recorded unreached, not a refusal) = 2 (T526, T601, individually verifiable); direction A (recorded fail, real refusal) = 5 (T615/T616/T617/T621/T622, the 2026-08-22 Claude session-limit cohort, cross-confirmed by T612's hand annotation); ~79 further rows flagged by the classifier across the 2026-08-20 keeper/memory-pressure era are NOT individually recoverable (accumulated logs, launch-only run records) — an upper bound, not a count.
